# The actions directive (org.owasp.csrfguard.action.*) gives the user the ability to specify one or more
# actions that should be invoked when a CSRF attack is detected. Every action must implement the
# org.owasp.csrfguard.action.IAction interface either directly or indirectly through the
# org.owasp.csrfguard.action.AbstractAction helper class. Many actions accept parameters that can be specified
# along with the action class declaration. These parameters are consumed at runtime and impact the behavior of
# the associated action.
#
# The syntax for defining and configuring CSRFGuard actions is relatively straight forward. Let us assume we wish
# to redirect the user to a default page when a CSRF attack is detected. A redirect action already exists within
# the CSRFGuard bundle and is available via the class name org.owasp.csrfguard.actions.Redirect. In order to enable
# this action, we capture the following declaration in the Owasp.CsrfGuard.properties file:
#
# syntax: org.owasp.csrfguard.action.[actionName] = [className]
# example: org.owasp.csrfguard.action.class.Redirect = org.owasp.csrfguard.actions.Redirect
#
# The aforementioned directive declares an action called "Redirect" (i.e. [actionName]) referencing the Java class
# "org.owasp.csrfguard.actions.Redirect" (i.e. [className]). Anytime a CSRF attack is detected, the Redirect action
# will be executed. You may be asking yourself, "but how do I specify where the user is redirected?"; this is where
# action parameters come into play. In order to specify the redirect location, we capture the following declaration
# in the Owasp.CsrfGuard.properties file:
#
# syntax: org.owasp.csrfguard.action.[actionName].[parameterName] = [parameterValue]
# example: org.owasp.csrfguard.action.Redirect.ErrorPage = %servletContext%/error.html
#
# The aforementioned directive declares an action parameter called "ErrorPage" (i.e. [parameterName]) with the value
# of "%servletContext%/error.html" (i.e. [parameterValue]) for the action "Redirect" (i.e. [actionName]). The
# Redirect action expects the "ErrorPage" parameter to be defined and will redirect the user to this location when

rows.title: TRUNK-6768: Remove unused BOM entries and ban SNAPSHOT dependencies in release builds
rows.excerpt:
actual module usage, removes unused managed entries, and adds a release-build check that fails on SNAPSHOT dependencies.

Changes:

### 1. BOM Audit (`bom/pom.xml`, `web/pom.xml`)

Audited every managed dependency in `bom/pom.xml` against what `api`, `web`, `webapp`, and `liquibase` actually declare or resolve (via `mvn dependency:tree`).

**Removed (confirmed unused anywhere in the module tree):**
- `org.openmrs.liquibase.ext:type-converter` — confirmed unused via dependency:tree across all modules

**Kept, with explanatory comments** (per the ticket's "deliberately provided with a comment" criterion):
- `jaxen` — required transitively by the `liquibase` module for XML changelog XPath support; not declared by `api`/`web`/`webapp`
- `netty-bom` — pins the Netty version pulled in transitively via the AWS SDK S3 client
- `sonar-jacoco-listeners` — used as a listener dependency for the jacoco-maven-plugin / Sonar coverage integration in the root pom.xml, not a direct project dependency

### 2. Release-build check for SNAPSHOT dependencies (`pom.xml`)

Added a `release` Maven profile using the built-in `banDynamicVersions` Enforcer rule, bound to the `validate` phase, which fails the build if any resolved dependency has a SNAPSHOT version, a version range, or a LATEST/RELEASE placeholder.

Tested:
- `mvn validate -pl api` → passes (normal dev builds unaffected)
- `mvn validate -Prelease -pl api` → fails with a precise message naming the offending SNAPSHOT dependency

### 3. What's NOT included, and why

The ticket also asks for milestone (`-M`), alpha, beta, and RC qualifiers to be banned in release builds. I was unable to implement this with `bannedDependencies` (the rule the ticket suggests) or any other built-in Enforcer rule:

- `banDynamicVersions` only covers SNAPSHOT, version ranges, and LATEST/RELEASE — milestone/alpha/beta/RC versions are not "dynamic" by Maven's definition and are explicitly out of scope for this rule.
- `bannedDependencies`' wildcard support only replaces a *whole* segment (groupId, artifactId, or version) or accepts a real Maven version range. It does not support partial substring matching within the version field (e.g. `*-M*`). I verified this directly: testing both a `regex:`-prefixed pattern and a plain wildcard pattern against this version position either matched nothing, or — more concerningly — mat

rows.excerpt:
deprecation call sites, and the README has a forUri migration section #130.
  • fix: the JSP and Jakarta bundles now declare the core version they need ([1.5,2), because the tags call Encode.forJson) and the JSP API ranges they support, instead of unversioned imports that could wire to an older core and fail when a tag ran. Bundle symbolic names are now declared explicitly and unchanged #137.
  • fix: forHtmlUnquotedAttribute now replaces U+0085 (NEL) with a hyphen like the other C1 control characters, instead of emitting &[#133](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder/issues/133);, which HTML5 parsers decode as U+2026 #136.
  • fix: the XML 1.1 encoders (forXml11, forXml11Content, forXml11Attribute) now encode U+0085 (NEL) as … and U+2028 (line separator) as  , so they are not normalized to a line feed #136.
  • maintenance: clarify output-context contracts and expand XML 1.1 tests, fix clean reactor compilation, and remove the obsolete benchmark profile.
